question.worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-7$ into the right-hand-side gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-14\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5},$ then $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-14\pi )=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}-10\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-14\pi )+1=-10(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{5})+1=2\sqrt{3}+1.\end{aligned}
$$
